tip: In the definite, the adjective takes -a and the noun keeps its ending: det goda kaffet (the good coffee).
Use den before en-words and det before ett-words: den nya läraren (the new teacher), an en-word.
With an ett-word the past participle adds -t: riset är tillagat (the rice is cooked).
Add -t to an adjective to make an adverb: försiktig becomes försiktigt (carefully) here.
The adjective adds -a when the subject is plural: vi är glada (we are happy).
glad att plus an infinitive says what you are glad to do: glad att träffa dig (glad to meet you).
Nationality adjectives stay lowercase in Swedish: svenska (Swedish), never capitalized.
Ha is the imperative of ha (to have), used in wishes like ha en bra dag (have a nice day).
Make a command negative by putting inte after the verb: glöm inte (don't forget).
sluta plus a plain infinitive means stop doing something: sluta prata (stop talking).
Swedish uses the definite for body parts, not a possessive: tvätta händerna (wash your hands).
lägga sig is reflexive and means lie down or go to bed: lägg dig (go to bed).
In the particle verb värma upp (heat up), the stress falls on upp: vi värmer upp maten.
The verb se ut (to look) splits and wraps the description: ser hotfullt ut (looks threatening).
skjuta upp is a particle verb meaning postpone: jag skjuter upp beslutet (I postpone the decision).
The reflexive ta för sig means help yourself to food: ta för dig (help yourself).
An att-clause can act as the subject of the sentence: att han kom (that he came) surprised me.
In an embedded question the subject stays before the verb: när hon kommer (when she comes), no inversion.
Inside an att-clause, adverbs like aldrig come before the verb: att hon aldrig skulle glömma.
When a clause comes first, the main verb goes before its subject: hinner vi (we make it).
som om plus a past verb means as if: som om tiden stod stilla (as if time stood still).
kommer att plus an infinitive expresses the future: kommer att gå bra (will go well).
Vad plus an adjective forms an exclamation: vad roligt (how nice).
The -s ending can make a verb reciprocal: ses means see each other, as in vi ses.
Adding -s forms the passive: bjuds means is offered, as in bjuds jag på fika.
You can drop som when it is the object of the relative clause: boken jag läser (the book I read).
för att plus an infinitive means in order to: för att hämta (to pick up).
så att introduces purpose, meaning so that: så att vi kan börja (so that we can start).
Use i with compass directions: i norr (in the north), likewise i söder, öster, väster.
hit means to here and marks motion, unlike the static här: kom hit (come here).
